subject: Logic
title: State Your Claim Clearly
description: A 60-second lesson on State Your Claim Clearly.

hook.text: We should probably maybe consider thinking about doing something about pollution. What are you actually arguing?

buildup.text: A strong argument starts with a clear, specific claim. Vague claims can't be supported or challenged.

discovery.text: Good claims are falsifiable—they stick their neck out and say something concrete that could be proven wrong.

twist.text: People keep claims vague on purpose—it's harder to be wrong when you haven't actually said anything.

climax.text: Before arguing, write your conclusion in one clear sentence. If you can't, you don't know your own argument.

punchline.text: Say what you mean or mean nothing.

quiz.question: Why should a claim be specific and falsifiable?
options: So it can be properly supported or challenged
So no one disagrees with it
